MINUTES
  REGULAR PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, OCTOBER 6, 2025

1.  CALL TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order by CHAIR OLSON at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

CHAIR OLSON led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Olson, Nicklas, Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli,
  Schachter, Yoo

  City Staff Present: Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst
  Katrina Kawagoe, Senior Planner
  Cameron Hall, Assistant Planner

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES,
  SEPTEMBER 8, 2025

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR NICKLAS to,

  APPROVE THE CORRECTED ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 8, 2025.

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250337; ADDRESS: 1 Sweetgrass Lane, Rolling
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Yehudah Younessian; DESCRIPTION: A request
  for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-250338) and approval of a
  Grading application (G-250339) for the demolition of three existing non-compliant
  structures and retaining walls, installation of compliant retaining walls and associated
  grading to stabilize the slope.

  1
Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
October 6, 2025
 Commissioner Repp-Loadsman recused herself from this item due to the proximity of a
property she owns to the subject property.

Assistant Planner Hall presented Planning Application No. PA-250337 summarizing the staff
report. The proposed project includes the demolition of multiple structures that were built
within a Southern California Edison (SCE) easement including a 696 SF open patio cabana
which was built on the property line, a 332 SF non-habitable two-story structure which was
built closer than three feel from the property line, a 472 SF non-compliant two story structure,
existing non-compliant retaining walls, and non-compliant stairs. The demolition will require
associated grading at the southeastern slope, and to stabilize the exposed slope, two new
sections of retaining walls will be installed at the eastern portion of the property.

Assistant Planner Hall stated that staff have determined that this project meets the criteria
for Neighborhood Compatibility.

Assistant Planner Hall stated the Planning Commission approve PA-250337, subject to the
conditions outlined in the staff report.

CHAIR OLSON asked if there was a mechanism in place notifying a buyer if the property is
in non-compliant status. Director Naughton stated that there is a pre-sale application that is
required prior to the sale of a property in the City.

Grant Govel, 22 Harbor Sight Drive, stated that his property is adjacent to the subject site.
He stated that he has concern with the shared retaining fence between the properties and
asked that this fence also be repaired.

CHAIR OLSON asked if there had been any discussion about this fence with the property
owner. Assistant Planner Hall stated that he has not, but is open to discussing this with the
property owner.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR, Mr. Govel stated that he has
discussed this with the property owner, and he has agreed that he would like to resolve this
and move forward.

Further discussion ensued regarding the location of the fence.

Director Naughton asked Mr. Govel to contact staff after the meeting to discuss a resolution
for the fence repair and to provide photos of the fence.

VICE CHAIR NICKLAS asked Mr. Govel if he discussed this with the property owner and if
the property owner agreed to repair the fence. Mr. Govel stated that yes, the property owner
agreed verbally.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE PA-250337, SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS OUTLINED IN THE
  STAFF REPORT.

Ayes: Olson, Nicklas, Medawar, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
Noes:
Absent:
Abstain: Repp-Loadsman

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application
No. PA-250337, a request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination and approval of
a Grading application for the demolition of three existing non-compliant structures and
retaining walls, installation of compliant retaining walls and associated grading to stabilize
the slope at 1 Sweetgrass Lane. There is a 20-day appeal period by which any member of
the public or the Council by its own motion, may appeal this project.

  2
Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
October 6, 2025
 8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250160; ADDRESS: 758 Silver Spur Road (Barte
  Earle Way), Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Mostafa Rahimi;
  DESCRIPTION: A request to amend a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-250159) for
  medical office use, to include oxygen therapy services, a Precise Plan of Design
  (PPD-250161) for exterior improvements including the installation of related medical
  equipment, and a Variance (V-250162) to provide fewer than the minimum required
  number of parking spaces.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that staff misidentified information on the plans which led to
an error in the public notice. The public notice for this item will be recirculated to a 500’ radius
of the subject property and republished in the newspaper.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommend that the Planning Commission
continue Planning Application No. 250160 to the meeting scheduled for November 3, 2025.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 250160 TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING SCHEDULED FOR NOVEMBER 3, 2025.

Ayes: Olson, Nicklas, Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
Noes:
Absent:
Abstain:

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250272; ADDRESS: 6 Branding Iron Lane,
  Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Gregory George, StudioGWG;
  DESCRIPTION: A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-
  250273) and a Variance (V-250274) for the installation of two fences that are greater
  than two (2) feet in height within the front yard setback.

Senior Planner Kawagoe presented Planning Application No. PA-250272 summarizing the
staff report. She stated that this home has a unique orientation by which the property is
almost entirely enclosed on all four sides. Access to the property is achieved by way of a
private road between 4 and 12 Branding Iron Lane. She stated that the west side of the
property will have a sliding gate with access to the property and the east side will have a
wood fence.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that staff has determined that this project meets the criteria
for Neighborhood Compatibility and staff can support the request for a Variance.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommend that the Planning Commission open
the public hearing, take public testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and
adopt Resolution No. PA-250272, approving the project.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

Greg George, Architect, stated that this is a unique property and explained the reasoning for
the gate and fence and stated that since they share a long driveway, the lights from
approaching vehicles will shine into the house. He stated that they have addressed access
issues with the Fire Department.

In response to a question from Commissioner Romanelli, Senior Planner Katrina confirmed
that notifications were sent to a 500’ radius of the subject site and staff received no
responses.

  3
Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
October 6, 2025
 COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

VICE CHAIR NICKLAS made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN
to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250272 AS PRESENTED.

Ayes: Olson, Nicklas, Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
Noes:
Absent:
Abstain:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application
No. PA-250272, a request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination and a Variance
for the installation of two fences that are greater than two (2) feet in height within the front
yard setback for 6 Branding Iron Lane. There is a 20-day appeal period by which any member
of the public or the Council by its own motion, may appeal this project.

C.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240540; ADDRESS: 19 Rollingwood Drive,
  Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Riad Itani, Seaside Designs;
  DESCRIPTION: A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-
  240541) for rear yard improvements that include legalizing unpermitted retaining
  walls, a Grading Permit (G-240542) for the export of more than 20 cubic yards of earth
  materials and excavation greater than three feet in vertical height at its deepest point,
  and a Variance (V-250301) to allow a retaining wall within two feet of a property line.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that the applicant, Mr. Itani, is a friend and customer;
however, he sees no conflict of interest in reviewing this application.

Senior Planner Kawagoe presented Planning Application No. PA-240540 summarizing the
staff report. She stated that in November of 2024, staff received an application for a pool;
however, it was discovered that some work had already taken place which led to staff
opening a code enforcement case for this property. Since then, staff have been working with
the applicant regarding the height of the walls and their proximity to the property line. In
addition to having built walls that were not compliant with the city’s code, the applicant also
built a wall into a slope easement to accommodate the pool. To protect the City against any
liability, the property owner signed a hold harmless agreement, which is also included as a
condition of approval. Senior Planner Kawagoe further explained the height and location of
the retaining walls and free-standing walls. She also stated that grading for the project
includes a maximum 6.5 FT in depth of fill and a cut with the maximum of 5.8 FT in depth.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that staff determined that the project meets the criteria for
Neighborhood Compatibility. This project also meets the criteria for grading except for a
section of the wall that is less than two feet from the property line on the east side of the
property for which a Variance is being requested. She stated that staff can support the
request for a Variance.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that the Planning Commission open the public hearing, take
public testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and adopt Resolution No. PA-
240540, approving the project.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Senior Planner Kawagoe
stated that there are walls that are not in compliance with the code, and the proposed project
will bring the walls into compliance with the code.

CHAIR OLSON asked if construction within an easement has been allowed previously with
a hold harmless agreement. Director Naughton stated that this is one of the first instances in
at least the last ten years where there has been a proposal to construct within a slope
  4
Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
October 6, 2025
 easement. The reason for this agreement is to protect the public right-of-way and was the
recommendation from the City Attorney’s office. The agreement has been executed and it
will need to be recorded.

In response to a question from CHAIR OLSON, Director Naughton explained that there are
specific criteria on what can or cannot be built within an easement. For this project, there are
no specific requirements recorded for this slope easement; staff assumes that this was to
protect the public right-of-way since the slopes were uncompacted fill.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that easements are sometimes recorded to
preserve areas for future utilities; however, in this case it may be to prevent structures from
being built within the easement due to the uncompacted fill. She added that from her
perspective if there is oversight via a building permit and proper design, then it is just up to
the Planning Commission to determine that it meets appropriate standards.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if the applicant had submitted this proposal prior to
commencing any work, would this have been presented to the Planning Commission for
consideration. Director Naughton stated that the application would have been before the
Planning Commission for the grading portion, not for the Variance.

CHAIR OLSON asked about the drainage plan which shows that the drainage water is
discharging onto the city trail. Director Naughton stated that the drainage will need to meet
low impact development standards.

CHAIR OLSON expressed his concern with the walls having a negative visual impact on the
neighborhood; he added that the grading is excessive. He also stated that the soils report
indicates that the walls were built on fill and noted that the walls need to be underpinned.

COMMISSIONER  MEDAWAR  made  a  motion,  seconded  by  COMMISSIONER
SCHACHTER to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

Riad Itani, Architect, stated that when he became involved with this project the area was
already graded, and the walls were already built; he stated that the property owner had hired
licensed civil and structural engineers. He stated that this project will meet all the engineering
standards, from fully designed walls and fully compacted soil. He stated that the multiple
retaining walls are due to the City’s five-foot height limit requirement. He stated that the
structural details show that the footings and the thickness of the retaining walls are above
and beyond the design criteria.

CHAIR OLSON stated that the soils report still requires underpinning. Mr. Itani stated that
this is not the case anymore. He stated that Mr. Tony Lee, Engineer, will be going to the site
to take more samples to be sure that the compaction meets the requirement of 94% density.
Mr. Itani noted that Mr. Lee stamped the plans for the retaining walls, which were reviewed
and approved after the soils report that was provided.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR
to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

COMMISSIONER YOO stated that he would like to have a better understanding of the rights
the City may be giving up by approving this application. He also expressed his concern with
retroactively approving an application where there is a violation and that may have been
approved if the applicant had taken the proper steps.

  5
Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
October 6, 2025
 COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that a current soils report should be submitted. He
also expressed his concern with retroactively approving applications and noted that these
are huge improvements.

CHAIR OLSON stated that if this project had been presented prior to construction that it is
likely that the Planning Commission would not approve construction within an easement. He
also has issue with the drainage plan.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that his concern is that the walls are safe and that the
drainage be properly designed. He stated that regarding aesthetics, he did not see an issue.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN inquired that if the Variance was not approved, then
they would have to reconstruct a portion of the wall to push it back, so that it meets the two
foot setback requirement from a property line. Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that they
could reconstruct it, however it would change the circulation around the pool.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER requested information on why this was constructed without
permits, who the contractor was, and the types of licenses they hold.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
SCHACHTER to,

  CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240540 TO THE PLANNING
  COMMISSION MEETING SCHEDULED FOR NOVEMBER 3, 2025 IN ORDER FOR
  THE APPLICANT TO CLARIFY THE ISSUES THAT WERE RAISED AT THIS
  MEETING AND FOR STAFF TO PROVIDE FURTHER DETAIL IF THE VARIANCE
  WAS NOT SUPPORTED.

Ayes: Olson, Nicklas, Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
Noes:
Absent:
Abstain:

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

NONE

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, SEPTEMBER 9, 2025

B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR OLSON adjourned the meeting at 8:26 p.m. to the next regular Planning Commission meeting
on Monday, November 3, 2025 at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes
Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Larry Olson, Chair

  6
Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
October 6, 2025
